---CRITIQUE Accounting-Aligned Physical Payoff Balance---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Since OIADP ≡ OIBDP − DP by construction, the only change from the archived "Physical-Capital Payoff Balance Value" is subtracting ΔDP from the numerator of the incremental-payoff leg — a cosmetic tweak to the strongest archived signal (and a leg already used verbatim in "Enterprise-Cash Post-Depreciation Payoff"), so it is effectively a rediscovery rather than a new mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Multi-Year Physical Payoff Balance---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Still the same three-leg architecture as the archived cash/physical-payoff winner, but moving the payoff term to a three-year profit change over cumulative depreciation is a genuine horizon change that tests whether the result reflects durable capital productivity rather than one-year noise, and it is a defensible (if incremental) refinement.

---CRITIQUE Persistent-Liquidity Physical Payoff---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: TS_MIN(che,3) is very highly correlated with current cash for most firms, so this is a low-information perturbation of the archived best signal stacked on top of the already-cosmetic post-depreciation relabeling, and any performance change will be hard to attribute to the stated "durable liquidity" mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Post-Depreciation Profit Surprise Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Because SUB(oibdp,dp) is identically oiadp, this reduces to Δ(operating income)/market cap × ROA — i.e., the archived "Organizational Profit Surprise Value" (fmb 0.86) with the second leg's denominator changed from xsga to at, and both legs are direct restatements of the well-known earnings-change/price and profitability anomalies.

---CRITIQUE Smoothed Innovation Profit Trend Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Replacing DELTA(·,1) with TREND(·,3) in the archived "Innovation Profit Surprise Value" is a textbook smoothing variant with no new economic content; the turnover argument is plausible but turnover is not among the evaluation metrics, so this is a cosmetic re-run of an already-successful signal.

---CRITIQUE Cash-Realized Innovation Surprise---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Adding an operating-cash-ROA hurdle to the archived innovation-surprise signal is an economically motivated test of whether the R&D-adjusted profit growth is cash-realized rather than an artifact of the capitalization adjustment, though it is a recombination of archived components and risks trimming coverage without changing the driving leg.
